findings.text: Each season from 2017-2026, Locksmith only used bet rules that had already worked in earlier seasons, then graded them at the line each rule would have bet (the closing line, or the SportsBookReview opener for opening-line rules; prices assumed). Record: 562-482-21, 53.8% wins, +34.3 units (+3.2% return). Our stricter certificate test (Python and R, every season, only information known in time) rates all 5 NFL bet types a tie with the market so far, so none is shown as proven. Backtests are past games, not live bets.

findings.title: Locksmith's NFL numbers tie the market, so we show the market's
findings.text: Over 3,417 past games our blended margin missed the final score by 9.92 points on average and the closing line by 9.92: a tie, and most of that blend is the closing line itself. Tested on 2,616 NFL games the model never saw: our projected margin was not proven better than the closing spread (better in 3 of 10 seasons, not enough to count). We show the market's number.

findings.title: Early-week totals: a hint of where the line moves, not a proven bet
findings.text: Locksmith's early-week model anticipates part of the move from the opening total to the close (past games, 2014-2020 openers). Tested on 1,349 NFL games the model never saw: our early projected total was not proven better than the opening total (better in 5 of 5 seasons, not enough to count). We show the market's number.

findings.title: Home favorites are slightly overpriced
findings.text: Since 2006 home favorites covered only 48.0% of the time (3,403 games). Sportsbooks shade these lines because the public loves favorites. Small edge, best as a tiebreaker.

findings.title: Sportsbooks under-react to wind (past games)
findings.text: Each mph of wind above 10 lowers scoring by about 0.38 points, but the line only moves 0.09. That was measured with the wind actually observed at kickoff, which nobody knows days ahead, so wind unders are only suggested inside 48 hours of kickoff. Tested on 266 NFL bets the model never saw: our chances on these bets were not proven better than the price at game time (better in 4 of 6 seasons, not enough to count). The test also used something you could not know in time (picks games using kickoff wind). We show the market's number.

findings.title: QB injury news is priced correctly
findings.text: When a starting quarterback changes, sportsbooks move the line about the right amount. No edge there.

findings.title: Public-betting tricks don’t reliably work
findings.text: On 917 real games with actual betting percentages, betting against the side a book is ‘holding’ won 51%, following reverse line moves won 49%. You need 52.4% to profit. These are shown for context only.

findings.title: Two betting-percentage signals worth watching
findings.text: When big bettors pile onto a total (money far above ticket count), that side won 55% of 240 games, and fading 70%+ of the public on spreads won 55%. Promising but not proven yet.

findings.title: Player projections beat ‘last six games’ where it matters
findings.text: Tested on every 2025 game: passing yards miss 59 yards versus 67 for a simple recent average, and touchdown odds are far better calibrated. For catches, targets and rushing, recent usage is about as good as anything.

findings.title: The score simulator is honest about uncertainty
findings.text: Real final scores landed inside Locksmith’s ‘80% likely’ range 82% of the time, and it reproduces how often games end on 3 and 7.

findings.title: Most edges disappear by kickoff
findings.text: Locksmith’s numbers can anticipate part of a line's move but do not beat the closing line, and the ‘early total’ bets lost money when bought late. Line-move bets (away side / under when the model expects the line to move that way) only make sense at the opener, so they are suggested only when Locksmith captures a real opener itself.

findings.title: Popular betting angles are already priced in
findings.text: Referees, Thursday games, division games, prime time, altitude and teams playing on their body clock all showed no edge against the closing line.
